name: Meross Smart Wi-Fi Plug MSS210 (EU)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11 b/g/n) with one internal antenna.

matter.note: Meross's EU page and spec sheet list HomeKit, Alexa, Google and SmartThings but not Matter, and we found no CSA listing. Only a Meross UK shop page for the MSS210HK mentions Matter, so we leave it unconfirmed.

apple_home.note: Sold as HomeKit (MSS210HK) and non-HomeKit versions under one name. Meross's shop says only the HomeKit version supports Apple Home; the EU product page lists HomeKit without separating them. Check for the HomeKit label.

google_home.note: Meross lists Google Assistant; works by linking your Meross account.

alexa.note: Meross lists Amazon Alexa; works through the Meross skill linked to your Meross account.

smartthings.note: Meross lists SmartThings; works by linking your Meross account in the SmartThings app.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant has no official Meross integration. Owners use community add-ons (HACS), and the HomeKit version may pair via HomeKit Device, but neither is documented for this model.

hubRequired.note: Meross says no hub is needed; it connects to your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.

localControl.note: Meross doesn't say whether it works without internet. The HomeKit version should run locally in Apple Home, but we found no Meross page confirming it.

energyMonitoring.note: Meross's EU spec lists 'Energy Monitor: No'. Meross sells metering plugs as separate models (e.g. MSS210PZF, MSS310).

maxLoadWatts.note: Meross rates the EU/FR version at 16 A max but gives no wattage. At 230 V that would be about 3680 W.

summary: The Meross MSS210 (EU) is a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plug with no hub, rated 16 A. Meross lists Alexa, Google Assistant and SmartThings, which work by linking your Meross account. Apple Home depends on the variant: Meross sells HomeKit (MSS210HK) and non-HomeKit versions under the same name. It has no energy monitoring.
caveats: Sold in HomeKit and non-HomeKit versions; only the HomeKit version (MSS210HK) works with Apple Home.
No official Home Assistant integration; owners rely on community add-ons.
